notes: Sources: 2018_01 collective agreement; 2018_02 tenure and promotion documents. Both are governing documents (the 2015-2018 YUFA collective agreement and its companion volume, which Art. 13.01 makes part of the agreement), cover term 1 May 2015 - 30 April 2018, in force on the reference date 2018-02-26.

Group covered: "Employee" = member of the YUFA bargaining unit = all full-time faculty (professorial and alternate streams) and full-time librarians and archivists in every Faculty, including Science, Lassonde School of Engineering and LA&PS: main_campus_tenure_stream. Post-Doctoral Visitors are in the unit but governed by Appendix A Schedule A instead of Article 19 (c22-c30, own faculty_group). SSHRC Canada Research Fellows are covered only by Arts. 19.01, 19.02, 19.05, 19.07, 19.14 (Appendix A C).

Chain, birth parent: pregnancy leave 17 (c1, full salary) -> parental leave 35 (c3; first 5 weeks EI parental supplemented to 100% by c4 from week 2 of c3; EI parental c8 from week 2 of c3, 35 weeks at 55%) -> discretionary additional unpaid leave up to 12 for the health of the primary caregiver (c7). Sick leave (c9/c10, 15 weeks) and the incapacity leave (c13, up to 4 years) are unlinked.

Chain, non-birth parent: primary care giver leave 17 (c2, full salary) -> parental leave 35 (c3; c4 top-up 5 weeks; EI c8); OR, for a parent who does not have principal responsibility, paid parental leave 4 (c5) -> unpaid parental leave 35 (c6). The two paths are linked in_lieu_of (c5-c2, c6-c3, c4-c5) because they are exclusive by caregiver status (19.10: "does not qualify to receive pregnancy or primary care giver leave"). Art. 19.11: if both parents are employees they may share their paid periods of leave.

No EI maternity benefit is named for faculty (19.08(a) pays full salary for the pregnancy leave with no EI reference); EI is named only for the parental-leave supplement, so the EI component is the parental benefit with the one-week wait served at the start of the parental claim (R21).

Tenure clock: D.2.4 gives a one-year probationary extension on request to those who qualify for pregnancy or primary care giver leave (c16). Art. 19.12: pregnancy, paid parental, parental and primary care giver leave accrue years of service credit as if on site (so the clock runs during the leave; the extension is separate). Probationary appointments last up to six years (12.05; D.2.3).

Not components: 19.08 "An employee shall, if she so chooses, have the right to continue with her regular duties during pregnancy" (a right to keep working, not leave, pay, relief or accommodation); 19.17 court leave, 19.18 terminal leave, 19.19 educational leave, 19.20-19.27 political leave, Article 20 sabbatical, 18.15 research release, Appendix L Research Development Fellowships, Appendix O graduate supervision credits (purposes unrelated to a birth); Appendix G and 26.15 childcare centre support; Appendix A Schedule A bereavement leave.

Cross-references not saved: LTSCP / Long-Term Disability Salary Continuance Insurance plan terms (26.10, Appendix D); the statement of the terms and levels of benefits (26.01) and the Benefits Booklet (Appendix N); JCOAA recommendations on modifying sabbaticals for illness or pregnancy (19.16); "Employee Accommodation Process" / Employee Accommodation Protocol (18.42); University Policies on Workplace Harassment and Workplace Violence (18.38); York University Relocation Expenses Procedure (26.16); Supplemental Benefits Plan (26.05); York Pension Plan (26.02); unit teaching load documents (18.08.1); the CUPE 3903 Unit 2 collective agreement (12.31); Tri-Council Agency Framework (11.08). None of these is cited as setting a parental-leave provision.

No calendar is coded: the documents name the Autumn/Winter session and terms but state no term length in weeks or kind of term for teaching (R8). No leave_limits or cap_weeks_all_sources: 19.15(b) caps leaves of absence without pay at three years ("will not normally be approved"), recorded on c15, not as a per-event parental limit.
